title: Portable Checkpoints Can Reduce Completion
abstract: We study a procurement contract in which the incumbent privately learns its opportunity cost of completion after delivering a verifiable intermediate output that a replacement can use. Greater replacement availability raises expected surplus but can lower the probability of project completion: under the optimal contract, the completion bonus falls, inducing some incumbents to exit before they know whether a replacement is available. If availability is observed before exit and the bonus can depend on it, greater replacement availability never lowers the completion probability and raises it if and only if some incumbents would exit even when no replacement is available.
